key_concepts: [url]How to create procedural wall with blender geometry nodes^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b_vAUbQpHvI[/url]

content: Start with the default cube, adding a Geometry Nodes Modifier (Image 1).
The setup for random terrain involves noise, a map range to adjust the output, isolating the z-axis, and finally positioning the noise on a grid (Image 2).

The noise pattern is controlled by the [k]Noise Texture[/k] node. Change the Dimensions to 2D, since we only care about raising or lowering the terrain in the z-axis. Adjusting the Scale will zoom in or out on the noise pattern. Lowering or increasing the Detail and the Roughness will also smooth out or sharpen the texture.

The Factor output from the [k]Noise Texture[/k] node produces floating-point values between 0.0 and 1.0. If you look at the geometry output from the side, you see the Z values range from 0.0 to 1.0 (Image 3). If we want to change the terrain to go from a low point of -2.5 to a high of 5.0, we can do that by adjusting the To Min and To Max values (Image 4). We can set a flat top to the peaks by limiting the From Max value (Image 5). You can also create a flat floor by raising the From Min (Image 6).

Add two Bézier Curves to the scene and name them 'wall' and 'path' (Image 7). [k]Numpad7[/k] into Top View, select the wall curve, [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, and [k]X,V[/k] (Image 8). From the toolbar on the right, enable the [k]Draw[/k] tool and set the Depth to Surface (Image 9). In Solid Viewport Shading Mode draw a winding curve that our wall will follow (Image 10). Hide the wall curve and bring the it into our network and pin the network in place (Image 11).

Resample the curve so we get a point every 0.1m and convert it to a mesh (Image 12). We need to give some shape to our curve, so we will use a [k]Curve Line[/k] to give it some volume (Image 13). Change the [k]Curve Line[/k]'s Method to Direction, and set the Direction to -1 in the y-axis and 0 in the others (Image 14). Set the height of the wall with the Length field (Image 15).

Disconnect the terrain from the geometry output and turn on Wireframe Viewport Shading and X-Ray Mode; if you look at the wall mesh we see vertical faces only (Image 16). Duplicate the [k]Resample Curve[/k] node to the [k]Curve Line[/k] network and we will see horizontal lines added to the wall  mesh (Image 17).

We will add stones randomly to the wall with a [k]Distribute Points on Faces[/k] node (Image 18). Set the Distribution Method to Poisson Disk, the Distance Min to 0.4m and the Density Max to 1000.0 (Image 19). Add an [k]Instance on Points[/k] node we will use to add stones (Image 20).
We need stone building blocks for the wall. We will follow two possible methods for that

Add a [k]Cube[/k] node as our instance (Image 21). Lower the Scale on the [k]Instance on Points[/k] node until the stones are a good size (Image 22). Add a [k]Subdivision Surface[/k] node and increase the Edge Crease (Image 23). Add a [k]Random Value[/k] node to control the Scale (Image 24).
Control the stones' rotation with the [k]Distribute Points on Faces[/k] node's Rotation output (Image 25).

Draw the path curve going through the wall (Image 26). We will use the path to carve out a door in the wall, but first let's visualize the curve as a tunnel going through the wall (Image 27). Bring in a [k]Raycast[/k] node to read the tunnel's geometry and use any intersection with the wall as the Selection to send to the geometry output (Image 28). We want to invert the selection to make an opening, so add a [k]Separate XYZ[/k] and a [k]Greater Than[/k] node (Image 29). Play with the operation, changing it from greater than to less than, changing the Threshold and the circle's radius.

Duplicate the [k]Distribute Points on Faces[/k], [k]Random Value[/k], and [k]Instance on Points[/k] nodes and connect them to the tunnel to give it a rocky face (Image 30). We need to limit the distribution of stones to just those points close to the wall. Bring in a [k]Geometry Proximity[/k] node, set its Geometry input to the wall mesh and connect a [k]Less Than[/k] node to its Distance output (Image 31).

Now we need a stone pathway. Add in another [k]Curve to Mesh[/k] node for the path curve and this time use a curve line as the profile shape (Image 32). Change the Method to Direction and the Direction to 1.0m in the x-axis (Image 33). Look at the path going through the tunnel and adjust the Start input in the X direction until the path is in the center of the tunnel (Image 34).
